definition: Indoctrination means the teaching of a set of beliefs so thoroughly that they are accepted without question.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word indoctrination. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know indoctrination should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The sect's catechism ran to ninety questions, and indoctrination began with the first: every answer given word for word, or repeated until it was.

Instruction is far milder than indoctrination: it simply hands the material over — the manual, the drill, the theorem — and welcomes a raised hand; indoctrination teaches so thoroughly that the raised hands stop.
Brainwashing goes further than indoctrination — the indoctrinated student has stopped asking questions; the brainwashed one can no longer form them.

Conditioning trains automatic responses — the reflex, the habit, the flinch — answers the body gives before thought gets a vote. Indoctrination works one level up: it drills the thoughts themselves, until the beliefs feel like reflexes and questioning them no longer occurs to anyone.

Propaganda is the outward-facing campaign — posters and broadcasts aimed at strangers a movement hopes to sway. Indoctrination points the same machinery inward, drilling the movement's own members until the beliefs are held without question. Propaganda persuades outsiders; indoctrination trains insiders.
